title: 2016 AMC 10B Problem 10

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: A thin piece of wood of uniform density in the shape of an equilateral triangle with side length \(3\) inches weighs \(12\) ounces. A second piece of the same type of wood, with the same thickness, also in the shape of an equilateral triangle, has side length \(5\) inches. Which of the following is closest to the weight, in ounces, of the second piece?

solutions.text:
The surface area is increased by a factor of \(\frac 53 ^2 \) since the side lengths are increased by a factor of \(\frac 53.\) Also since the thickness is constant, the volume is scaled up by that much. Then, the wood having the same density makes the weight increase by a factor of \(\frac 53^2 \) as well, so the new weight is \[12 \cdot \dfrac {25}{9} = \dfrac{100}3.\] This is approximately \(33.3.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: Weights scale like areas because thickness and density are fixed
